api/Invex.SemanticVersion.SemVer.html.summary: Class SemVer Namespace Invex.SemanticVersion Assembly Invex.SemanticVersion.dll An immutable semantic version following the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification. Supports parsing, comparison, and conversion operations for version strings in the format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+METADATA]. [PublicAPI] public sealed class SemVer Inheritance object SemVer Examples var version1 = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha.1+build.123"); SemVer version2 = "2.0.0"; bool isNewer = version2 > version1; // true Remarks This class implements semantic version comparison where: Release versions (without pre-release) are greater than pre-release versions Pre-release versions are compared lexicographically by dot-separated identifiers Numeric identifiers in pre-release are compared numerically (of any length) and have lower precedence than alphanumeric identifiers Metadata is used only as a final tiebreaker when all other components are equal Create instances with Parse(string), TryParse(string?, out SemVer), FromSystemVersion(Version, bool) or the implicit conversion from string. The public parameterless constructor is obsolete: it always creates version 0.0.0 and cannot set components. The type implements System.ISpanParsable<TSelf>, System.IComparable<T> and System.Numerics.IComparisonOperators<TSelf, TOther, TResult>, so it works with generic parsing, sorting and ordered collections. System.Text.Json serializes a SemVer as an object with the Major, Minor, Patch, PreRelease and Metadata properties (null components are written as null) and deserializes it through a private constructor, without a custom converter. The computed properties Prefix, IsPreRelease, BuildNumberFromPreRelease and BuildNumberFromMetadata are not serialized. Constructors SemVer() Initializes a new instance of the SemVer class representing version 0.0.0. [Obsolete("Use SemVer.Parse, SemVer.TryParse, SemVer.FromSystemVersion or SemVer.One instead. This constructor always creates version 0.0.0 and will be removed in a future major version.")] public SemVer() Remarks This constructor was exposed unintentionally. All properties have private init accessors, so it cannot be used to set components; it always creates version 0.0.0. Properties BuildNumberFromMetadata Gets the build number extracted from the metadata. [JsonIgnore] public int BuildNumberFromMetadata { get; } Property Value int The numeric build number if exactly one number is found in the metadata; otherwise, 0 (including when Metadata is null). Examples SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build.99").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 99 SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 0 (no number) SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 0 (no metadata) Remarks This property applies the same rules as ExtractBuildNumber(string?) to the metadata string. Only returns a non-zero value if exactly one numeric sequence is present. Unlike ExtractBuildNumber(string?), it never throws: a single numeric sequence greater than int.MaxValue (for example a timestamp such as +20261014123045) also returns 0. BuildNumberFromPreRelease Gets the build number extracted from the pre-release identifier. [JsonIgnore] public int BuildNumberFromPreRelease { get; } Property Value int The numeric build number if exactly one number is found in the pre-release; otherwise, 0 (including when PreRelease is null). Examples SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-rc.42").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 42 SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 0 (no number) SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-1.2").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 0 (multiple numbers) SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 0 (no pre-release) Remarks This property applies the same rules as ExtractBuildNumber(string?) to the pre-release string. Only returns a non-zero value if exactly one numeric sequence is present. Unlike ExtractBuildNumber(string?), it never throws: a single numeric sequence greater than int.MaxValue also returns 0. IsPreRelease Gets a value indicating whether this version is a pre-release version. [JsonIgnore] public bool IsPreRelease { get; } Property Value bool true if PreRelease is not null; otherwise, false. Major Gets the major version number. public int Major { get; } Property Value int The major version number, indicating incompatible API changes. Metadata Gets the build metadata. public string? Metadata { get; } Property Value string The build metadata string without the leading plus sign, or null if no metadata is present. Remarks The specification ignores metadata when determining version precedence. This implementation uses it as a final tiebreaker (ordinal string comparison) in CompareTo(SemVer?) when all other components are equal, so versions that differ only in metadata are not equal. Minor Gets the minor version number. public int Minor { get; } Property Value int The minor version number, indicating backwards-compatible functionality additions. One Gets a semantic version representing version 1.0.0. public static SemVer One { get; } Property Value SemVer A SemVer instance with Major set to 1, Minor and Patch set to 0, and no pre-release or metadata. Patch Gets the patch version number. public int Patch { get; } Property Value int The patch version number, indicating backwards-compatible bug fixes. PreRelease Gets the pre-release version identifier. public string? PreRelease { get; } Property Value string The pre-release identifier string without the leading hyphen, or null if this is a release version. Remarks Pre-release identifiers are dot-separated and may contain alphanumeric characters and hyphens, for example alpha.1, rc.2 or beta. Prefix Gets the version prefix in the format "MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH". [JsonIgnore] public string Prefix { get; } Property Value string A string representing the core version without pre-release or metadata components. Examples SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha+build").Prefix; // "1.2.3" Methods CompareTo(SemVer?) Compares the current instance with another SemVer and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order. public int CompareTo(SemVer? other) Parameters other SemVer The SemVer to compare with this instance. Returns int A value that indicates the relative order of the objects being compared: Less than zero if this instance precedes other; Zero if they are equal; Greater than zero if this instance follows other. Remarks Comparison follows Semantic Versioning precedence rules: Compare major, minor, and patch versions numerically Pre-release versions have lower precedence than normal versions Pre-release identifiers are compared left to right: identifiers consisting only of ASCII digits are compared numerically (of any length, without overflow), a numeric identifier has lower precedence than an alphanumeric one, and alphanumeric identifiers are compared ordinally (ASCII) When all shared identifiers are equal, the version with more pre-release identifiers is greater Metadata is used only as a final tiebreaker (ordinal comparison) Any instance is greater than null, so this method returns a positive value when other is null. Equals(SemVer?) Determines whether the specified SemVer is equal to the current instance. public bool Equals(SemVer? other) Parameters other SemVer The SemVer to compare with the current instance. Returns bool true if CompareTo(SemVer?) returns zero, meaning all components including Metadata are equal; otherwise, false (including when other is null). Equals(object?) Determines whether the specified object is equal to the current instance. public override bool Equals(object? obj) Parameters obj object The object to compare with the current instance. Returns bool true if obj is a SemVer equal to the current instance according to Equals(SemVer?); otherwise, false. ExtractBuildNumber(string?) Extracts a single numeric value from the specified input string. public static int ExtractBuildNumber(string? input) Parameters input string The string to extract a number from. Returns int The numeric value if exactly one sequence of digits is found; otherwise, 0. Returns 0 if the input is null, empty, whitespace, or contains zero or multiple numbers. Examples SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("alpha.123"); // 123 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("SNAPSHOT-12"); // 12 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("beta"); // 0 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("1.2.3"); // 0 (multiple numbers) SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber(null); // 0 Remarks BuildNumberFromPreRelease and BuildNumberFromMetadata apply the same extraction rules to version components, except that they return 0 instead of throwing when the value is greater than int.MaxValue. This method can be called on any string. Exceptions OverflowException Thrown when the single sequence of digits is greater than int.MaxValue. FromSystemVersion(Version, bool) Creates a SemVer instance from a System.Version. public static SemVer FromSystemVersion(Version version, bool throwIfContainsRevision = false) Parameters version Version The System.Version to convert. throwIfContainsRevision bool If true, throws an exception when the version has a revision greater than zero. Defaults to false. Returns SemVer A SemVer with Major, Minor, and Patch (from Build) components and no pre-release or metadata. Remarks Maps System.Version Major.Minor.Build to SemVer Major.Minor.Patch. The revision component is ignored unless throwIfContainsRevision is true. An undefined System.Version.Build (-1, as in new Version(1, 2)) maps to a Patch of 0, so the result is always a valid version that ToSystemVersion(bool, bool) can convert back. Exceptions ArgumentException Thrown when throwIfContainsRevision is true and System.Version.Revision is greater than zero. GetHashCode() Serves as the default hash function. public override int GetHashCode() Returns int A hash code computed from Major, Minor, Patch, PreRelease and Metadata, consistent with Equals(SemVer?). IsBetween(SemVer, SemVer) Determines whether the current version is between two specified versions (exclusive). public bool IsBetween(SemVer firstBound, SemVer secondBound) Parameters firstBound SemVer The first boundary version. secondBound SemVer The second boundary version. Returns bool true if this version is strictly between the two bounds; otherwise, false. Examples var version = SemVer.Parse("1.5.0"); version.IsBetween("1.0.0", "2.0.0"); // true version.IsBetween("2.0.0", "1.0.0"); // true (bounds in any order) version.IsBetween("1.0.0", "1.5.0"); // false (bounds are exclusive) Remarks Both bounds are exclusive and may be supplied in any order; the lower one is determined with the same precedence rules as CompareTo(SemVer?), so pre-release and metadata in the bounds are respected. If both bounds are equal, returns true only if this version equals the bounds. Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char>, IFormatProvider?) Parses a span of characters representing a semantic version. public static SemVer Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char> s, IFormatProvider? provider) Parameters s ReadOnlySpan<char> The span of characters to parse. provider IFormatProvider Ignored; parsing is culture-independent. Returns SemVer A SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s. Remarks This overload implements System.ISpanParsable<TSelf>. The span is converted to a string and parsed with Parse(string, IFormatProvider?). Exceptions ArgumentException Thrown when s is not a valid semantic version string. OverflowException Thrown when the major, minor or patch component is greater than int.MaxValue. Parse(string) Parses a string representation of a semantic version. public static SemVer Parse(string s) Parameters s string The string to parse. Returns SemVer A SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s. Examples var version = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha.1+build.456"); Remarks Accepts version strings in the format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+METADATA] where MAJOR, MINOR, and PATCH are non-negative integers without leading zeros. Use TryParse(string?, out SemVer) when the input may be invalid. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when s is null. ArgumentException Thrown when s is not a valid semantic version string. OverflowException Thrown when the major, minor or patch component is greater than int.MaxValue. Parse(string, IFormatProvider?) Parses a string representation of a semantic version. public static SemVer Parse(string s, IFormatProvider? provider) Parameters s string The string to parse. provider IFormatProvider Ignored; parsing is culture-independent. Returns SemVer A SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s. Remarks This overload implements System.IParsable<TSelf>. Input is validated with the regular expression suggested by the Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification, so leading zeros in numeric components and empty pre-release or metadata segments are rejected. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when s is null. ArgumentException Thrown when s is not a valid semantic version string. OverflowException Thrown when the major, minor or patch component is greater than int.MaxValue. ToString() Returns the string representation of this semantic version. public override string ToString() Returns string A string in the format MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+METADATA], where the pre-release and metadata components are included only if present. Examples SemVer.Parse("1.2.3").ToString(); // "1.2.3" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha").ToString(); // "1.2.3-alpha" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3+build.1").ToString(); // "1.2.3+build.1" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha+build.1").ToString(); // "1.2.3-alpha+build.1" Remarks For a version obtained by parsing, the result round-trips: parsing it again with Parse(string) produces an equal version. ToSystemVersion(bool, bool) Converts this semantic version to a System.Version instance. public Version ToSystemVersion(bool throwIfContainsPreRelease = false, bool throwIfContainsMetadata = false) Parameters throwIfContainsPreRelease bool If true, throws an exception when pre-release data is present. Defaults to false. throwIfContainsMetadata bool If true, throws an exception when metadata is present. Defaults to false. Returns Version A System.Version with Major, Minor, and Build (from Patch) components. Remarks Maps SemVer Major.Minor.Patch to System.Version Major.Minor.Build. Pre-release and metadata information is lost in the conversion. Exceptions ArgumentException Thrown when throwIfContainsPreRelease is true and pre-release data is present, or when throwIfContainsMetadata is true and metadata is present. ArgumentOutOfRangeException Thrown when Major, Minor or Patch is negative, which can only happen for an instance deserialized from JSON containing negative components. TryParse(ReadOnlySpan<char>, out SemVer) Tries to parse a span of characters representing a semantic version. public static bool TryParse(ReadOnlySpan<char> s, out SemVer result) Parameters s ReadOnlySpan<char> The span of characters to parse. result SemVer When this method returns, contains the SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s if the conversion succeeded, or null if it failed. Returns bool true if s was converted successfully; otherwise, false. Remarks Never throws; returns false for invalid input, including components greater than int.MaxValue. TryParse(ReadOnlySpan<char>, IFormatProvider?, out SemVer) Tries to parse a span of characters representing a semantic version. public static bool TryParse(ReadOnlySpan<char> s, IFormatProvider? provider, out SemVer result) Parameters s ReadOnlySpan<char> The span of characters to parse. provider IFormatProvider Ignored; parsing is culture-independent. result SemVer When this method returns, contains the SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s if the conversion succeeded, or null if it failed. Returns bool true if s was converted successfully; otherwise, false. Remarks This overload implements System.ISpanParsable<TSelf>. The span is converted to a string and parsed with TryParse(string?, IFormatProvider?, out SemVer). TryParse(string?, out SemVer) Tries to parse a string representation of a semantic version. public static bool TryParse(string? s, out SemVer result) Parameters s string The string to parse. result SemVer When this method returns, contains the SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s if the conversion succeeded, or null if it failed. Returns bool true if s was converted successfully; otherwise, false. Remarks Never throws; returns false for invalid input, including components greater than int.MaxValue. TryParse(string?, IFormatProvider?, out SemVer) Tries to parse a string representation of a semantic version. public static bool TryParse(string? s, IFormatProvider? provider, out SemVer result) Parameters s string The string to parse. provider IFormatProvider Ignored; parsing is culture-independent. result SemVer When this method returns, contains the SemVer equivalent to the version contained in s if the conversion succeeded, or null if it failed. Returns bool true if s was converted successfully; otherwise, false. Remarks This overload implements System.IParsable<TSelf> and never throws: it returns false when s is null, is not a valid semantic version string, or has a major, minor or patch component greater than int.MaxValue. Operators operator ==(SemVer?, SemVer?) Determines whether two versions are equal. public static bool operator ==(SemVer? left, SemVer? right) Parameters left SemVer The first version to compare, or null. right SemVer The second version to compare, or null. Returns bool true if both are null, or if left is not null and Equals(SemVer?) returns true; otherwise, false. Remarks This operator is null-safe and, like Equals(SemVer?), takes metadata into account. operator >(SemVer?, SemVer?) Determines whether left has higher precedence than right. public static bool operator >(SemVer? left, SemVer? right) Parameters left SemVer The version to compare, or null. right SemVer The version to compare against, or null. Returns bool true if left compared with right using CompareTo(SemVer?) gives a value greater than zero; otherwise, false. Remarks This operator is null-safe: null precedes every version and two null operands are equal, consistent with CompareTo(SemVer?). operator >=(SemVer?, SemVer?) Determines whether left has the same or higher precedence than right. public static bool operator >=(SemVer? left, SemVer? right) Parameters left SemVer The version to compare, or null. right SemVer The version to compare against, or null. Returns bool true if left compared with right using CompareTo(SemVer?) gives a value greater than or equal to zero; otherwise, false. Remarks This operator is null-safe: null precedes every version and two null operands are equal, consistent with CompareTo(SemVer?). implicit operator string(SemVer) Converts a SemVer to its string representation. public static implicit operator string(SemVer semVer) Parameters semVer SemVer The SemVer to convert. Must not be null. Returns string The string representation of the semantic version, as returned by ToString(). Examples string text = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3"); // "1.2.3" implicit operator SemVer(string) Converts the string representation of a semantic version to its SemVer equivalent. public static implicit operator SemVer(string s) Parameters s string The string representation of the semantic version. Returns SemVer A SemVer object equivalent to the version contained in s. Examples SemVer version = "1.2.3-rc.1"; Remarks Calls Parse(string), so invalid input throws. Use TryParse(string?, out SemVer) when the input may be untrusted. Exceptions ArgumentNullException Thrown when s is null. ArgumentException Thrown when s is not a valid semantic version string. OverflowException Thrown when the major, minor or patch component is greater than int.MaxValue. operator !=(SemVer?, SemVer?) Determines whether two versions are not equal. public static bool operator !=(SemVer? left, SemVer? right) Parameters left SemVer The first version to compare, or null. right SemVer The second version to compare, or null. Returns bool true if the versions are not equal according to the equality operator; otherwise, false. Remarks This operator is null-safe. operator <(SemVer?, SemVer?) Determines whether left has lower precedence than right. public static bool operator <(SemVer? left, SemVer? right) Parameters left SemVer The version to compare, or null. right SemVer The version to compare against, or null. Returns bool true if left compared with right using CompareTo(SemVer?) gives a value less than zero; otherwise, false. Remarks This operator is null-safe: null precedes every version and two null operands are equal, consistent with CompareTo(SemVer?). operator <=(SemVer?, SemVer?) Determines whether left has the same or lower precedence than right. public static bool operator <=(SemVer? left, SemVer? right) Parameters left SemVer The version to compare, or null. right SemVer The version to compare against, or null. Returns bool true if left compared with right using CompareTo(SemVer?) gives a value less than or equal to zero; otherwise, false. Remarks This operator is null-safe: null precedes every version and two null operands are equal, consistent with CompareTo(SemVer?).

api/index.html.title: API Reference | Invex.SemanticVersion
api/index.html.summary: API Reference Invex.SemanticVersion exposes a single public type; this reference is generated from its XML documentation. Invex.SemanticVersion Type Kind Description SemVer sealed class An immutable Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version with parsing, precedence comparison, string and System.Version conversions and System.Text.Json support. Members at a glance Member Description Major, Minor, Patch Core version components. PreRelease, Metadata Optional pre-release and build-metadata segments (nullable). Prefix "MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH" without pre-release/metadata. IsPreRelease true when a pre-release identifier is present. BuildNumberFromPreRelease / BuildNumberFromMetadata Single numeric value extracted from the respective segment, otherwise 0; throws OverflowException if that value exceeds int.MaxValue. SemVer.One Convenience instance for 1.0.0. Parse / TryParse String and ReadOnlySpan<char> parsing (ISpanParsable<SemVer>); Parse throws OverflowException when a core component exceeds int.MaxValue, TryParse returns false. CompareTo, Equals, comparison operators SemVer-compliant precedence and equality. IsBetween Exclusive, order-independent range check. ToSystemVersion / FromSystemVersion Conversion to and from System.Version. ExtractBuildNumber Static helper to pull a single number from a string. Implicit conversions string to SemVer (parses, throws on invalid input) and SemVer to string. Typical flow using Invex.SemanticVersion; if (SemVer.TryParse(input, out var version) && version >= "2.0.0") Console.WriteLine($"Supported: {version.Prefix}"); For task-oriented guides, start with the Introduction.

docs/build-numbers.html.title: Build Number Extraction | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/build-numbers.html.summary: Build Number Extraction SemVer provides helpers to extract a single numeric value from a pre-release or metadata string. This is useful when CI/CD systems embed a build counter in a pre-release tag (e.g. 1.0.0-rc.42) and you need that number programmatically. BuildNumberFromPreRelease Returns the build number embedded in the pre-release identifier. SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-rc.42").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 42 SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.1227").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 1227 SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-SNAPSHOT-7").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 7 Returns 0 when: There is no pre-release identifier (PreRelease == null). The pre-release contains no numeric sequence. The pre-release contains more than one numeric sequence (ambiguous). SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 0 — no pre-release SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 0 — no number SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-1.2.3").BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 0 — multiple numbers BuildNumberFromMetadata Identical behaviour, but reads from the metadata segment instead: SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build.99").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 99 SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build.1").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 1 Returns 0 in the same edge cases as BuildNumberFromPreRelease. SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 0 — no metadata SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+sha.abc").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 0 — no number SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+1.2").BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 0 — multiple numbers ExtractBuildNumber(string? input) — static helper The static ExtractBuildNumber method applies the same extraction rules as both properties above, except that it throws instead of returning 0 when the number overflows (see the note below). You can call it directly on any arbitrary string: SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("rc.42"); // 42 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("alpha.123"); // 123 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("SNAPSHOT-12"); // 12 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("7"); // 7 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("beta"); // 0 — no number SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("alpha.beta"); // 0 — no number SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("1.2.3"); // 0 — multiple numbers SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber("alpha3.4valid"); // 0 — multiple numbers SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber(null); // 0 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber(""); // 0 SemVer.ExtractBuildNumber(" "); // 0 Rules Condition Return value null, empty, or whitespace 0 Exactly one numeric sequence found That number Zero or more than one numeric sequence 0 Note A single numeric sequence larger than int.MaxValue makes ExtractBuildNumber throw OverflowException. The BuildNumberFromPreRelease and BuildNumberFromMetadata properties never throw; they return 0 in that case, for example for timestamp metadata such as 1.0.0+20261014123045. Practical example A CI pipeline writes a version like 1.0.0-rc.{BUILD_NUMBER}. After reading the version from a config file you can extract the build counter back out: var version = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-rc.42"); int buildNumber = version.BuildNumberFromPreRelease; // 42 Console.WriteLine($"This is release candidate build #{buildNumber}"); Or when the build number lives in metadata: var version = SemVer.Parse("2.3.0+build.1337"); int buildNumber = version.BuildNumberFromMetadata; // 1337 See also System.Version Interop Parsing SemVer

docs/changelog.html.title: Changelog | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/changelog.html.summary: Changelog All notable changes to Invex.SemanticVersion are documented here. This project adheres to Semantic Versioning. Unreleased Changed Pre-release precedence now follows SemVer 2.0.0 §11.4 exactly: numeric identifiers of any length are compared numerically (previously identifiers larger than int.MaxValue were compared as strings), numeric identifiers always have lower precedence than alphanumeric ones (previously 1.0.0-9 > 1.0.0-10a and 1.0.0-1 > 1.0.0--1), and identifiers such as -1 are no longer parsed as negative numbers. The ordering operators <, <=, > and >= are null-safe: null precedes every version, so a null left operand no longer throws NullReferenceException. FromSystemVersion maps an undefined Version.Build (-1, as in new Version(1, 2)) to a Patch of 0 instead of -1, so ToSystemVersion no longer throws on the result. BuildNumberFromPreRelease and BuildNumberFromMetadata return 0 instead of throwing OverflowException when the single number is larger than int.MaxValue. ExtractBuildNumber still throws in that case. Parsing accepts only ASCII digits. Non-ASCII Unicode digits (for example 1٣.0.0) previously made Parse throw FormatException, or were accepted inside pre-release identifiers. Now Parse throws ArgumentException and TryParse returns false. ExtractBuildNumber and the build number properties ignore non-ASCII digits. Parsing rejects a trailing newline (for example "1.0.0\n"), which was previously accepted. Parse now throws ArgumentException and TryParse returns false. Deprecated The public parameterless constructor SemVer(). It always creates 0.0.0; use Parse, TryParse, FromSystemVersion or One instead. Removed The .NET 8.0 and .NET 9.0 targets. The package now targets .NET 10.0 only. The unused System.IO.Abstractions package dependency. 1.0.0 — Initial Release Added SemVer sealed class implementing ISpanParsable<SemVer>, IComparable<SemVer>, and IComparisonOperators<SemVer, SemVer, bool>. Properties: Major, Minor, Patch, PreRelease, Metadata, Prefix, IsPreRelease. Static constant SemVer.One (1.0.0). Parse(string) — throwing parse from string. TryParse(string?, out SemVer?) — non-throwing parse from string. Parse(ReadOnlySpan<char>, IFormatProvider?) — throwing parse from span. TryParse(ReadOnlySpan<char>, IFormatProvider?, out SemVer?) — non-throwing parse from span. TryParse(ReadOnlySpan<char>, out SemVer?) — convenience span overload. Implicit conversions to/from string. CompareTo(SemVer?) — SemVer 2.0.0 compliant precedence comparison. Comparison operators: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=. Equals(SemVer?) and Equals(object?). GetHashCode() consistent with Equals. ToString() — canonical MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+METADATA] output. IsBetween(SemVer, SemVer) — exclusive, order-independent range check. ToSystemVersion(bool, bool) — convert to System.Version with optional guards. FromSystemVersion(Version, bool) — convert from System.Version with optional guard. BuildNumberFromPreRelease — extract single build number from pre-release. BuildNumberFromMetadata — extract single build number from metadata. ExtractBuildNumber(string?) — static helper to extract a single number from any string. System.Text.Json serialization support (all components serialized; computed properties excluded). Targets .NET 8.0, .NET 9.0, and .NET 10.0. See also Introduction Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 specification

docs/comparison.html.title: Comparison & Precedence | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/comparison.html.summary: Comparison & Precedence SemVer implements full SemVer 2.0.0 precedence rules via IComparable<SemVer> and IComparisonOperators<SemVer, SemVer, bool>. Read this page when you sort versions or check whether one version is newer than another. Precedence rules (summary) The ordering follows the SemVer 2.0.0 specification §11: Major is compared numerically — higher major wins. Minor is compared numerically when major is equal. Patch is compared numerically when major and minor are equal. Release > Pre-release — when core versions are identical a release version (no pre-release) has higher precedence than any pre-release. Pre-release identifiers are compared dot-by-dot left-to-right: If both identifiers consist only of digits they are compared numerically, whatever their length (10000000000 > 9999999999). A numeric identifier always has lower precedence than an alphanumeric one (1.0.0-9 < 1.0.0-10a). Two alphanumeric identifiers are compared lexically (ordinal, ASCII order). A shorter identifier list is less than a longer one when all common identifiers are equal. Build metadata is not considered for precedence by the spec, but this implementation uses it as a final tiebreaker (ordinal comparison) when everything else is equal. CompareTo int result = SemVer.Parse("2.0.0").CompareTo(SemVer.Parse("1.0.0")); // > 0 int result = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").CompareTo(SemVer.Parse("1.0.0")); // 0 int result = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").CompareTo(SemVer.Parse("2.0.0")); // < 0 // null is always less than any instance int result = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").CompareTo(null); // > 0 This is compatible with List<T>.Sort(), Array.Sort(), SortedSet<T>, OrderBy, etc. Comparison operators All six standard comparison operators are supported: SemVer a = "2.0.0"; SemVer b = "1.0.0"; bool gt = a > b; // true bool gte = a >= b; // true bool lt = a < b; // false bool lte = a <= b; // false bool eq = a == b; // false bool neq = a != b; // true All six operators are null-safe. null sorts before every version, consistent with CompareTo, and two null operands are equal. SemVer? x = null; SemVer? y = null; bool bothNull = (x == y); // true SemVer? z = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0"); bool leftNull = (x == z); // false bool rightNull = (z == x); // false bool lower = x < z; // true — null precedes every version bool higher = z > x; // true bool nullsEqual = x <= y; // true Ordering examples Release beats pre-release SemVer.Parse("1.0.0") > SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha") // true SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha") < SemVer.Parse("1.0.0") // true Numeric pre-release comparison // 10 > 9 numerically (not "10" < "9" lexically) SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.10") > SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.9"); // true Numeric identifiers precede alphanumeric ones // A purely numeric identifier always has lower precedence than an alphanumeric one SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.1") < SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.beta"); // true SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-9") < SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-10a"); // true Lexicographic pre-release comparison // 'b' > 'a' — beta is newer than alpha SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-beta") > SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha"); // true Longer pre-release wins on tie // "alpha.1.2" has more identifiers than "alpha.1" SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.1.2") > SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha.1"); // true Build metadata as tiebreaker // All version components and pre-release are equal — metadata breaks the tie SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build.2") > SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build.1"); // true Sorting a collection var versions = new List<SemVer> { "2.0.0", "1.0.0", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1", }; versions.Sort(); // Result (ascending): 1.0.0-alpha, 1.0.0-alpha.1, 1.0.0-rc.1, 1.0.0, 2.0.0 Equals and GetHashCode Equals uses CompareTo under the hood, so equality respects SemVer rules (including metadata as tiebreaker): SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").Equals(SemVer.Parse("1.0.0")); // true SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+a").Equals(SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+b")); // false (metadata differs) SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").Equals(SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha")); // false GetHashCode is consistent with Equals — two equal SemVer instances always produce the same hash code. See also Range Checks Parsing SemVer

docs/getting-started.html.title: Getting Started | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/getting-started.html.summary: Getting Started This guide walks you from installation to your first working code in five minutes. Read it first if you are new to the library. Requirements Target Framework Minimum SDK .NET 10.0 .NET SDK 10 The package references JetBrains.Annotations, which NuGet restores automatically. Installation .NET CLI (recommended) dotnet add package Invex.SemanticVersion Package Manager Console (Visual Studio) Install-Package Invex.SemanticVersion PackageReference (csproj) <PackageReference Include="Invex.SemanticVersion" Version="*" /> Tip Replace * with the specific version you want to pin, e.g. 1.0.0. Namespace Everything lives in a single namespace: using Invex.SemanticVersion; In projects with ImplicitUsings enabled, the package adds this using as a global using for you. Quick Start using Invex.SemanticVersion; // ── Parsing ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── var version = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha.1+build.123"); Console.WriteLine(version.Major); // 1 Console.WriteLine(version.Minor); // 2 Console.WriteLine(version.Patch); // 3 Console.WriteLine(version.PreRelease); // alpha.1 Console.WriteLine(version.Metadata); // build.123 Console.WriteLine(version.Prefix); // 1.2.3 Console.WriteLine(version.IsPreRelease); // True Console.WriteLine(version); // 1.2.3-alpha.1+build.123 // ── Safe (non-throwing) parse ───────────────────────────────────────────── if (SemVer.TryParse("2.0.0-rc.1", out var candidate)) Console.WriteLine(candidate); // 2.0.0-rc.1 // ── Comparison ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── var stable = SemVer.Parse("2.0.0"); var prerelease = SemVer.Parse("2.0.0-rc.1"); Console.WriteLine(stable > prerelease); // True — release beats pre-release var versions = new List<SemVer> { "2.0.0", "1.0.0", "1.0.0-rc.1" }; versions.Sort(); // Result: 1.0.0-rc.1, 1.0.0, 2.0.0 // ── Implicit string conversion ──────────────────────────────────────────── SemVer v = "3.1.0"; // string → SemVer string text = v; // SemVer → string ("3.1.0") // ── Range check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── var v150 = SemVer.Parse("1.5.0"); Console.WriteLine(v150.IsBetween("1.0.0", "2.0.0")); // True (exclusive) // ── System.Version interop ──────────────────────────────────────────────── System.Version sysVer = SemVer.Parse("3.2.1").ToSystemVersion(); // 3.2.1 SemVer fromSys = SemVer.FromSystemVersion(new System.Version(1, 2, 3)); // 1.2.3 Next steps Parsing: all parsing overloads and validation rules. Comparison & Precedence: how SemVer ordering works. JSON Serialization: storing versions in settings files. API Reference: every property and method documented.

docs/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Invex.SemanticVersion gives .NET code a single immutable type for Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 versions. This page explains when it fits, the concepts it is built on, and the design choices that affect how it behaves. What it is Version strings such as 1.4.0-rc.2+build.77 look simple, but comparing them as strings is wrong ("1.10.0" < "1.9.0" lexically) and System.Version cannot hold the pre-release or build-metadata parts. SemVer parses these strings once into a typed, immutable value that knows the specification's precedence rules and fits into the base class library like a built-in type: it is parsable, comparable, sortable, convertible to and from string, and serializable with System.Text.Json. When to use it You read versions from CI variables, GitVersion output, tags, manifests or configuration and need to compare them correctly (minimum supported version, "is this newer", sorting release lists). You need the pre-release label or a build counter embedded in it, for example 1.0.0-rc.42. You store versions in JSON settings or pass them through APIs that expect string or System.Version. When not to use it Version ranges and floating versions. There is no range syntax such as [1.0, 2.0) or 1.*; IsBetween only checks an exclusive range between two concrete versions. Loose or non-SemVer input. Strings like v1.2.3, 1.2 or 1.2.3.4 are rejected. Normalize them first, or use FromSystemVersion for four-part .NET versions. Metadata-insensitive equality. The specification ignores build metadata for precedence; this library uses it as a final tiebreaker, so 1.0.0+a and 1.0.0+b are not equal. Compare Prefix and PreRelease yourself if you need the strict specification behavior. Key concepts at a glance Concept In one sentence Read more Components Major, Minor and Patch are integers; PreRelease and Metadata are optional strings without their - / + prefix. Parsing Precedence Core numbers first, then release over pre-release, then pre-release identifiers dot by dot, then metadata. Comparison & Precedence Conversions Implicit string conversions in both directions, plus explicit System.Version conversions with optional guards. String Conversion, System.Version Interop Build numbers A single number embedded in the pre-release or metadata can be read back as an int. Build Number Extraction Design principles One immutable type. Everything lives on SemVer; all properties are read-only after creation. Strict parsing. Input is validated with the regular expression suggested by the specification, so leading zeros and empty identifiers are rejected rather than silently accepted. BCL-native. SemVer implements ISpanParsable<SemVer>, IComparable<SemVer> and IComparisonOperators<SemVer, SemVer, bool>, so generic parsing, List<T>.Sort(), SortedSet<T> and operators work without adapters. Explicit about lossy conversions. ToSystemVersion and FromSystemVersion drop data silently by default but accept flags that throw instead. Stable public API. The public surface is locked by a snapshot test, so changes are always deliberate. Next steps Getting Started: install the package and parse your first version. Parsing Comparison & Precedence API Reference

docs/json-serialization.html.title: JSON Serialization | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/json-serialization.html.summary: JSON Serialization SemVer supports System.Text.Json out of the box. No custom converters or configuration are needed. Read this page when you store versions in settings files or exchange them over JSON APIs. Serialization using System.Text.Json; using Invex.SemanticVersion; var version = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha+build.1"); string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(version); Produces the following JSON object (shown indented for readability): { "Major": 1, "Minor": 2, "Patch": 3, "PreRelease": "alpha", "Metadata": "build.1" } The JSON representation stores each component as a named field. [JsonIgnore]-decorated computed properties (Prefix, IsPreRelease, BuildNumberFromPreRelease, BuildNumberFromMetadata) are excluded. Note Property names follow your JsonSerializerOptions. With the default options they are written as declared (Major, PreRelease, …) and matched case-sensitively when reading. With JsonSerializerDefaults.Web (the ASP.NET Core default) they are written in camelCase (major, preRelease, …) and matched case-insensitively. Deserialization string json = """{"Major":1,"Minor":2,"Patch":3,"PreRelease":"alpha","Metadata":"build.1"}"""; SemVer restored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<SemVer>(json)!; Console.WriteLine(restored); // 1.2.3-alpha+build.1 Console.WriteLine(restored.IsPreRelease); // True Round-trip guarantee A SemVer serialized and then deserialized always produces the same version string: var versions = new[] { "1.0.0", "1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0+build", "1.0.0-alpha+build", }; foreach (var v in versions) { var original = SemVer.Parse(v); var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(original); var restored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<SemVer>(json)!; Console.WriteLine(original == restored); // True for all Console.WriteLine(restored.ToString() == v); // True for all } Serializing null Nullable SemVer? properties serialize and deserialize as null in the standard JSON way: class MyConfig { public SemVer? MinVersion { get; set; } } var config = new MyConfig { MinVersion = null }; string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(config); // {"MinVersion":null} var restored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<MyConfig>(json)!; Console.WriteLine(restored.MinVersion is null); // True Embedding SemVer in larger objects class AppSettings { public SemVer Version { get; set; } = SemVer.One; public SemVer? RequiredMinVersion { get; set; } } var settings = new AppSettings { Version = "2.5.0", RequiredMinVersion = "2.0.0", }; string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(settings); // { // "Version": {"Major":2,"Minor":5,"Patch":0,"PreRelease":null,"Metadata":null}, // "RequiredMinVersion": {"Major":2,"Minor":0,"Patch":0,"PreRelease":null,"Metadata":null} // } AppSettings loaded = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<AppSettings>(json)!; Console.WriteLine(loaded.Version > loaded.RequiredMinVersion); // True See also String Conversion Getting Started SemVer

docs/parsing.html.title: Parsing | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/parsing.html.summary: Parsing Parsing turns a version string into a SemVer; use this page to choose between the throwing and non-throwing overloads and to see exactly which strings are accepted. SemVer accepts version strings in the canonical SemVer 2.0.0 format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+METADATA] Where: MAJOR, MINOR, and PATCH are non-negative integers with no leading zeros (except 0 itself). PRERELEASE is an optional dot-separated sequence of alphanumeric identifiers and hyphens. METADATA is an optional dot-separated sequence of alphanumeric identifiers and hyphens following +. Parse — throwing overload Use Parse when you expect the input to always be valid: SemVer v = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3"); SemVer v = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha"); SemVer v = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3+build.456"); SemVer v = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha.1+build.456"); Throws ArgumentException for any string that does not match the SemVer 2.0.0 grammar, ArgumentNullException for null, and OverflowException when MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH is larger than int.MaxValue. TryParse — non-throwing overload Use TryParse when the input may be invalid (user input, config files, etc.): if (SemVer.TryParse("1.0.0-rc.1", out var version)) { // version is valid — use it Console.WriteLine(version.PreRelease); // rc.1 } else { // string was not a valid SemVer } Returns false and sets result to null when parsing fails (including null input and components larger than int.MaxValue). Never throws. The IFormatProvider parameter of the ISpanParsable<SemVer> overloads is ignored; parsing is culture-independent. ISpanParsable<SemVer> — span overloads All parsing methods also accept ReadOnlySpan<char>, so SemVer works with generic code constrained to ISpanParsable<T>. The span is copied to a string before parsing: ReadOnlySpan<char> span = "1.0.0-beta".AsSpan(); // Throwing SemVer v = SemVer.Parse(span, null); // Non-throwing if (SemVer.TryParse(span, null, out var version)) { // ... } // Convenience overload without IFormatProvider if (SemVer.TryParse(span, out var version2)) { // ... } Valid and invalid examples Input Valid? Notes 1.0.0 ✅ Minimal release version 0.0.0 ✅ Zero version 10.20.30 ✅ Large version numbers 1.0.0-alpha ✅ Pre-release 1.0.0+build ✅ Build metadata only 1.0.0-alpha+build ✅ Pre-release + metadata 1.0.0-alpha.1+exp.sha.5114f85 ✅ Complex pre-release and metadata 1.0 ❌ Missing patch component 1.0.0.0 ❌ Four components (not SemVer) 1..0 ❌ Empty component 1.0.0- ❌ Empty pre-release 1.0.0+ ❌ Empty metadata -1.0.0 ❌ Negative major a.0.0 ❌ Non-numeric major Implicit parse via string assignment Because SemVer defines an implicit conversion from string, you can also write: SemVer v = "1.0.0-rc.1"; // calls Parse internally This uses the throwing Parse path, so an invalid string will throw ArgumentException. See String Conversion for details. What the parser validates Under the hood, SemVer uses the official SemVer 2.0.0 regular expression: ^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*) (?:-((?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[a-zA-Z-][0-9a-zA-Z-]*)(?:\.(?:0|[1-9]\d*|\d*[a-zA-Z-][0-9a-zA-Z-]*))*))? (?:\+([0-9a-zA-Z-]+(?:\.[0-9a-zA-Z-]+)*))?$ This ensures leading zeros are rejected (e.g. 01.0.0 is invalid) and all identifiers contain only the allowed character set. See also String Conversion Comparison & Precedence SemVer

docs/range-checks.html.title: Range Checks | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/range-checks.html.summary: Range Checks SemVer provides the IsBetween method for checking whether a version falls within an exclusive range. Use it for simple "newer than X but older than Y" checks between two concrete versions. IsBetween(SemVer firstBound, SemVer secondBound) Returns true if the current version is strictly between the two bounds (both bounds are exclusive). public bool IsBetween(SemVer firstBound, SemVer secondBound) Basic usage var v = SemVer.Parse("1.5.0"); v.IsBetween("1.0.0", "2.0.0"); // true — 1.0.0 < 1.5.0 < 2.0.0 v.IsBetween("1.0.0", "1.4.0"); // false — 1.5.0 is not below 1.4.0 v.IsBetween("1.5.0", "2.0.0"); // false — lower bound is exclusive v.IsBetween("1.0.0", "1.5.0"); // false — upper bound is exclusive Order-independent bounds The method accepts bounds in any order — the smaller value is automatically treated as the lower bound: var v = SemVer.Parse("1.5.0"); v.IsBetween("2.0.0", "1.0.0"); // true — same as IsBetween("1.0.0", "2.0.0") v.IsBetween("1.4.0", "1.0.0"); // false — 1.5.0 > 1.4.0 (upper bound) Equal bounds When both bounds are the same version, IsBetween returns true only if the version exactly equals the bounds: var v = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0"); v.IsBetween("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); // true — version == both bounds SemVer.Parse("2.0.0").IsBetween("1.0.0", "1.0.0"); // false Edge cases Scenario Result Version equals lower bound false (exclusive) Version equals upper bound false (exclusive) Version between bounds (ascending) true Version between bounds (descending) true Version below both bounds false Version above both bounds false Both bounds equal, version matches true Both bounds equal, version differs false Implicit string conversion in range checks Because SemVer supports implicit conversion from string, you can write range checks concisely: SemVer current = SemVer.Parse("1.5.0"); if (current.IsBetween("1.0.0", "2.0.0")) { Console.WriteLine("Version is in the 1.x range."); } Notes Both bounds use the same SemVer precedence rules described in Comparison & Precedence. Pre-release and metadata in the bounds are fully respected: var v = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-beta"); // 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0-beta < 1.0.0-rc.1 v.IsBetween("1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-rc.1"); // true See also Comparison & Precedence String Conversion IsBetween(SemVer, SemVer)

docs/string-conversion.html.title: String Conversion | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/string-conversion.html.summary: String Conversion SemVer provides bidirectional implicit conversions with string, and a deterministic ToString() implementation. Read this page when you pass versions to or from string-based APIs. ToString() Returns the canonical SemVer 2.0.0 string representation of the version. The output format is: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+METADATA] Pre-release and metadata segments are included only when they are non-null. SemVer.Parse("1.2.3").ToString(); // "1.2.3" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha").ToString(); // "1.2.3-alpha" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3+build.1").ToString(); // "1.2.3+build.1" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha+build.1").ToString(); // "1.2.3-alpha+build.1" ToString() is the inverse of Parse — a round-trip through Parse → ToString always returns the original string. Implicit conversion from string Assigning a string literal (or variable) to a SemVer variable calls Parse implicitly: SemVer version = "1.2.3-rc.1"; This is equivalent to: SemVer version = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-rc.1"); Warning The implicit conversion uses the throwing Parse path. An invalid string will throw ArgumentException. Use TryParse if the input may be untrusted. Practical uses // Method parameters void SetMinVersion(SemVer min) { /* ... */ } SetMinVersion("2.0.0"); // works // Collections var allowed = new HashSet<SemVer> { "1.0.0", "1.1.0", "2.0.0" }; // Comparison operators with literals SemVer current = SemVer.Parse("1.5.0"); bool tooOld = current < "2.0.0"; // true Implicit conversion to string Assigning a SemVer to a string variable calls ToString() implicitly: SemVer version = SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha+build.1"); string text = version; // "1.2.3-alpha+build.1" This is equivalent to: string text = version.ToString(); Practical uses // Storing in a string field string currentVersion = SemVer.Parse("3.0.0"); // Passing to string-accepting APIs Console.WriteLine(SemVer.Parse("1.0.0")); // ToString() called automatically File.WriteAllText("version.txt", SemVer.Parse("1.0.0")); // implicit to string Prefix The Prefix property returns only the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH part, omitting any pre-release or metadata: SemVer.Parse("1.2.3-alpha+build.1").Prefix; // "1.2.3" SemVer.Parse("1.2.3").Prefix; // "1.2.3" Useful when you need to compare or display only the numeric version core. See also Parsing JSON Serialization SemVer

docs/system-version-interop.html.title: System.Version Interop | Invex.SemanticVersion
docs/system-version-interop.html.summary: System.Version Interop SemVer provides two methods for converting between SemVer and the built-in System.Version type. Use them when you work with assembly versions or other APIs that only understand System.Version. Mapping between the two types SemVer component System.Version component Major Major Minor Minor Patch Build PreRelease (not representable) Metadata (not representable) (not present) Revision System.Version uses Build where SemVer uses Patch. Pre-release labels and build metadata have no equivalent in System.Version. ToSystemVersion Converts a SemVer instance to a System.Version: Version sysVer = SemVer.Parse("3.2.1").ToSystemVersion(); // sysVer.Major == 3, sysVer.Minor == 2, sysVer.Build == 1 Guard flags Pre-release and metadata are silently ignored by default. Pass the guard flags to throw instead: // throws ArgumentException — pre-release data would be lost SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha").ToSystemVersion(throwIfContainsPreRelease: true); // throws ArgumentException — metadata would be lost SemVer.Parse("1.0.0+build.1").ToSystemVersion(throwIfContainsMetadata: true); // both guards at once SemVer.Parse("1.0.0-alpha+build").ToSystemVersion( throwIfContainsPreRelease: true, throwIfContainsMetadata: true); // no pre-release or metadata — succeeds System.Version ok = SemVer.Parse("1.0.0").ToSystemVersion( throwIfContainsPreRelease: true, throwIfContainsMetadata: true); Parameter Type Default Behavior when true throwIfContainsPreRelease bool false Throws ArgumentException if PreRelease is non-null throwIfContainsMetadata bool false Throws ArgumentException if Metadata is non-null FromSystemVersion Creates a SemVer from a System.Version: SemVer v = SemVer.FromSystemVersion(new Version(1, 2, 3)); // v.Major == 1, v.Minor == 2, v.Patch == 3 // v.PreRelease == null, v.Metadata == null System.Version has a fourth Revision component that SemVer has no equivalent for. By default the revision is silently ignored: // revision (4) is ignored SemVer v = SemVer.FromSystemVersion(new Version(1, 2, 3, 4)); // v.Patch == 3 Note A System.Version created without a build component, such as new Version(1, 2), has Build == -1. That undefined build maps to Patch == 0, so SemVer.FromSystemVersion(new Version(1, 2)) is 1.2.0. Guard flag Pass throwIfContainsRevision: true to opt into strict mode: // throws ArgumentException — revision would be lost SemVer.FromSystemVersion(new Version(1, 2, 3, 4), throwIfContainsRevision: true); // revision is zero — succeeds SemVer ok = SemVer.FromSystemVersion(new Version(1, 2, 3, 0), throwIfContainsRevision: true); Parameter Type Default Behavior when true throwIfContainsRevision bool false Throws ArgumentException if Revision > 0 Common patterns Loading assembly version as SemVer using System.Reflection; var asm = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly(); var sysVer = asm.GetName().Version!; SemVer semVer = SemVer.FromSystemVersion(sysVer); Console.WriteLine(semVer); // e.g. "2.1.0" Comparing assembly version against a minimum SemVer current = SemVer.FromSystemVersion(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().GetName().Version!); SemVer minimum = "2.0.0"; if (current < minimum) throw new InvalidOperationException($"Assembly version {current} is below the required minimum {minimum}."); See also Build Number Extraction Comparison & Precedence SemVer
